subject: Telemetry heatmap & proposed observability test plan for Stratos Health
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@stratoshealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Telemetry heatmap & proposed observability test plan for Stratos Health

Hi Emily — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to iterate.

TL;DR: Stratos wants deterministic latency visibility and token-level cost attribution. Hyperscaler comparisons matter for you because of vendor lock and trace fidelity — we recommend a two-week, instrumented pilot with a small dedicated pool so we can produce apples-to-apples 95th percentile numbers and run the KV-cache effectiveness tests you asked about.

Key call notes (short):
- Primary objectives: 95th p90 latency at conversational payloads, token-level cost breakdown (embedding + generation), and end-to-end traceability across frontend -> Redwood -> backend services.
- Concern: tracing gaps from RPCs in some hyperscaler endpoints; you'd like an approach that preserves parent/spans for the entire request path.
- Success metrics: p95 latency under 350ms for typical 512-token window, trace span coverage >= 95%, and cache hit rate > 40% on repeated prompts.

Proposed observability test plan (high level):
1) Instrumented synthetic run (2h steady-state) with representative prompt distribution (we'll share generator).
2) OpenTelemetry end-to-end trace capture (sample at 100%) + token-level event logs for 1% sample of requests.
3) KV-cache efficacy: replay a 10k convo subset to measure cache hit improvement and per-token CPU/GPU time.
4) Streaming/UX smoke: 50 concurrent sessions with streaming enabled to verify tail latencies and partial-response behavior.
5) Comparative matrix: run same tests against your hyperscaler option (if you agree) to highlight trace gaps and deviations.

Attachments: redwood-ops-test-plan-v1.pdf (high-level steps), comparator-matrix.csv (schema for results).

Asks / next steps:
- Please confirm who from infra should join the technical deep-dive (we recommend your infra lead + SRE).
- If you want deterministic numbers, we recommend a short paid pilot on Dedicated capacity — Ben included with pricing notes below can put together a two-week estimate.
- Proposed slot for deep-dive: Jul 9 or Jul 12, 10:00-11:00 PT.

If that looks right, we'll iterate the test plan and lock the deep-dive.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com

--

Date: 2026-07-02T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry heatmap & proposed observability test plan for Stratos Health

Thanks, Sergio — this is exactly the level of detail we wanted. A few clarifying Qs before we lock dates: 

1) Trace overhead: you propose 100% OTLP sampling for the pilot. Can you confirm expected overhead on p95 latency when sampling at that level vs 10%? If we see a 10–20% tail impact we may not accept it for user-facing sessions.

2) Data retention & residency: our compliance team needs a short note on what metadata Redwood stores for traces and how long temporary token-level logs are retained.

3) Hyperscaler comparison: we can run the same suite against our incumbent vendor (we'll need a read-only account). Are there specific instrument-level differences we should expect (e.g., lost span propagation on Google Load Balancers)?

Carlos (infra) is on the thread now — Carlos, can you confirm time availability for a deep-dive the week of Jul 6 or Jul 13? We prefer Jul 9 but are flexible.

We'll also need a lightweight SOW for the two-week pilot (scope + acceptance criteria + pricing). Can Ben start a draft?

Thanks — Emily
Emily Chen
Head of Platform Engineering | Stratos Health
emily.chen@stratoshealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily.chen@stratoshealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-03T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Telemetry heatmap & proposed observability test plan for Stratos Health

Nice notes, Sergio — a few ops/implementation points I want to make so we present a tighter test plan: 

- OTLP sampling at 100% for a pilot is fine for short windows but yes, it will add overhead. In our experience, 100% tracing with span export increases the p95 by ~6–12% on A10s and ~10–18% on older T4-like configs, depending on exporter batching. We'll include an exporter-batching config in the plan so Emily can see trade-offs.

- Recommend we add a synthetic traffic profile (attached generator config) that includes 15% long-context chats (>1k tokens) to stress attention kernels. That will surface kernel selection differences across vendors.

- OpenTelemetry notes: Redwood supports OTLP/OTel and we add an extra token-level event stream for 1% of requests to capture per-token timings without shipping every token for all traffic. We'll share otlp-integration-notes.txt with the exact env vars and header mappings (attached).

- Hyperscaler differences to call out in the deep-dive: some vendors terminate trace context at the load balancer layer or have proprietary batching that collapses spans. We'll demo a small end-to-end trace showing lost parent/span when routed through those proxies.

- Resource ask: pilot should run on a small dedicated pool (2 x A10 equiv) for stable tail numbers. If budget's tight we can run on 4 x T4 with the caveat that p95 will be more variable.

I'll prepare a short tech appendix for the deep-dive showing the exporter configs and sample trace screenshots.

Marissa Cole
Staff Engineer, Observability | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

If you prefer a T4-based pilot the infra line drops to ~$6,500 but expect higher p95 variance.
